desc: This domain requires no argument about whether the government funds anomalous research, because the answer is a matter of public record for twenty-three years. Beginning in 1972 at Stanford Research Institute under Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ, and running through Army and DIA programmes known successively as Grill Flame, Center Lane, Sun Streak and finally Star Gate, the United States paid for controlled experiments in anomalous cognition and for operational intelligence tasking based on them. Puthoff and Targ published in Nature in October 1974; the programme's internal protocols, including the 1978 'Standard Remote Viewing Protocol', were later declassified; and thousands of pages sit in the CIA's electronic reading room. The programme was terminated in 1995 following an external evaluation, and CIA's public position is that it produced nothing of operational value - a denial that is itself a data point given the twenty-three-year expenditure. The relevance here is structural rather than substantive: the same principal investigators, the same institute, and in several cases the same individuals reappear in the AAWSAP era three decades later. Scoring high on this domain means an entity ran, funded, participated in or evaluated that work.

timeline.text: Harold Puthoff and Russell Targ begin remote viewing work at Stanford Research Institute under federal sponsorship. The programme runs through Grill Flame, Center Lane, Sun Streak and Star Gate until 1995, establishing beyond argument that the US government funds research of this kind for decades at a time before terminating it and denying it produced anything.
